newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LIFE STYLE-FRESKO'S ADDS SALAD TO VILNIUS CUISINE SCENE.
newsitem.headline: LIFE STYLE-FRESKO'S ADDS SALAD TO VILNIUS CUISINE SCENE.

text.p: The cuisine is definitely not Lithuanian, but just about everything else at Fresko's is.

Newly opened in Vilnius old town hall, Fresko's boasts a 300-year-old fresco in the centre dining room, a bar made of Lithuanian oak and theatre memorabilia suggesting a glorious history in drama earlier this century in Lithuania.
With entrees ranging from 26 litas to 29 litas and appetisers from 4.50 litas to 9.00 litas, Fresko's prices are above average for Vilnius, but you can do worse.
The restaurant also has several salads to serve as meals.
Some of the notable entrees are steak au poivre (28 litas) veal in mustard and cream sauce (27 litas), chicken taragon (29 litas) and salmon steak (28 litas).
The smoked salmon, at 10 litas, is a little plain. Even as an appetiser, the servings could be bigger.
The three colour salad is a better choice with a mix of lettuce and greens, red pepper, cabbage, onion, tomato, excellent croutons (unheard of in Lithuania) and creamy Italian dressing.
Portions are generous and the salad is presented attractively.
Vegetarians take note: the three colour salad is enough for a main course lunch but probably not for dinner.
The three colour is an impressive salad for Vilnius, worth the 12 litas price and a truly a significant event in Lithuanian salad history.
There is also a salad bar. But at 9 litas a trip, better load up.
It's nice to see a dish like chicken taragon on the menu, but the sauce can be watery and needs work.
The chicken portions are substantial but thin.
The salmon steak, on the other hand, deserves high marks. But with the restaurant just opened, features like sauces seem to change as the menu develops.
One of Fresko's drawing cards is atmosphere. Its bright interior adds to the charm of the place and provides a nice setting for a meal or casual glass of beer or wine.
Wines range in price from about 40 litas to 180 litas a bottle, with Chateuneuf du Pape '95 at the top.
The bar serves local favourite Utenos on tap (7 litas a pint) and some European and North American beers by the bottle.
